title: Dense-open localization
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $C$ be a reduced separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim C\le1$ (a reduced curve, as in [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]). Let $r$ be a prime number and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $C_{\Et}$, i.e. an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] with $rF=0$, which is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]; in particular $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair. Then:

1. There is a dense open subscheme $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ which is a finite disjoint union $U=\coprod_{a=1}^nU_a$ of irreducible open subschemes $U_a$ (each a reduced irreducible separated $k$-scheme of finite type of dimension $\le1$), such that $j^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant].
2. The closed complement $Z=C\setminus U$, with its reduced induced structure and closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], is zero-dimensional (a finite, possibly empty, set of closed points), and the sequence
$$
 0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0
$$
of extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and inverse image, whose maps are the counit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and the unit of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$, is exact.
3. Let $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow C$ be the composite open immersion. Then
$$
 \mathcal C(C,F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C(C,j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))\text{ for every }a,
$$
where, for a curve coefficient pair $(C,G)$, $\mathcal C(C,G)$ is the conjunction of the eight assertions $\mathcal C_1(C,G),\dots,\mathcal C_8(C,G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], each an implication that is true when its hypotheses (on $C$: affine, proper; on $G$: constructible, prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, $p$-primary) fail, as in Stacks, Situation 0A52.

proof.text: Generic constancy (Stacks, proof of Theorem 03SC, third paragraph: "By definition this means there is a dense open $U\subset X$ such that $\mathcal F|_U$ is finite locally constant"). By [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion] there is a finite partition $C=\coprod_{k<m}C_k$ into locally closed constructible subsets on each of which $F$ is locally constant with finite stalks. Give each $C_k$ its reduced induced subscheme structure with immersion $\iota_k:C_k\to C$; then $(C_k,\iota_k)_{k<m}$ is a stratification of $C$ in the sense of [def-constructible-stratification] (finitely many pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets covering $C$, each the image of an immersion), and each $\iota_k^{-1}F$ is locally constant with finite geometric stalks, i.e. finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant], [def-constructible-finite]. Hence $F$ is constructible in the sense of [def-constructible-constructible] (coefficients in $\mathbf F_r$-modules), and [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] gives a dense open $U'\subseteq C$ with $F|_{U'}$ finite locally constant. (The constructible-chapter nodes used here are finished in Lean on slopmaster2, state closed: tools, not route.)

Shrinking to disjoint irreducible pieces (Stacks, proof of Theorem 03SC, third paragraph: "after shrinking $U$, $U=U_1\amalg\dots\amalg U_n$ is a disjoint union of irreducible schemes (just remove the closed points which lie in the intersections of $\ge2$ components of $U$)"). $C$ is of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian, so it has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\dots,C_n$, with generic points $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$ (Mathlib: TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents). (a) $U'$ contains every $\eta_a$: the set $C_a\setminus igcup_{b
e a}C_b$ is open and contains $\eta_a$ (if $\eta_a\in C_b$ then $C_a\subseteq C_b$, so $a=b$); the dense $U'$ meets it in a point $y$, and $y\in\overline{\{\eta_a\}}$ with $U'$ open forces $\eta_a\in U'$. (b) For $a
e b$, $C_a\cap C_b$ is a closed subset of $C_a$ not containing $\eta_a$, hence a proper closed subset of the irreducible Noetherian space $C_a$ of dimension $\le1$, hence of dimension $0$: a finite set of closed points. Let $U=U'\setminus igcup_{a
e b}(C_a\cap C_b)$, open, containing all $\eta_a$, hence dense. Put $U_a=U\cap C_a$. The $U_a$ cover $U$, are pairwise disjoint and closed in $U$; being finitely many, each is also open in $U$ (complement of the union of the others). $U_a$ is a nonempty open subset of the irreducible $C_a$, hence irreducible; as an open subscheme of $C$ it is reduced, separated, of finite type over $k$ and of dimension $\le1$. So $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is a dense open with $U=\coprod_aU_a$. Finally $j^{-1}F=(F|_{U'})|_U$ is finite locally constant: if $\{V_i	o U'\}$ is an etale covering on which $F|_{U'}$ is constant with finite value, then $\{V_i	imes_{U'}U	o U\}$ is an etale covering of $U$ on which $j^{-1}F$ is constant with the same values [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]; likewise each $F|_{U_a}$ is finite locally constant.

The complement is zero-dimensional (Stacks, proof of Lemma 0GJA, first sentence: "Since $X'$ is dense, we see that $Z=X\setminus X'$ has dimension $0$ and hence is a finite set of $k$-rational points"). $Z=C\setminus U$ is closed and contains no generic point $\eta_a$ (step 2). A point $z\in Z$ lies in some $C_a$ with $z\ne\eta_a$, so $\overline{\{z\}}$ is a proper irreducible closed subset of $C_a$, which has dimension $\le1$; hence $\overline{\{z\}}=\{z\}$ and $z$ is a closed point. $Z$ is a closed subset of the Noetherian space $C$, so it has finitely many irreducible components, each the closure of a point, i.e. a closed point; thus $Z$ is a finite discrete set of closed points and its reduced induced subscheme, with closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], has dimension $0$ (or is empty).

The exact sequence. $U$ is the open complement of the closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] (Stacks Lemma 095L), applied to the sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules $F$, gives the exact sequence $0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ with the counit and the unit as maps. This proves parts 1 and 2 of the statement.

proof.text: Restriction to the dense open (Stacks, proof of Theorem 03SC, third paragraph: "By Lemma 0GJA we reduce to the case $\mathcal F=j_!\mathcal G$"). $F$ is killed by $r$, hence torsion, and constructible, and $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is the inclusion of a dense open subscheme; so [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-dense-open] (Stacks Lemma 0GJA) gives $\mathcal C(C,F)\Leftrightarrow\mathcal C(C,j_!j^{-1}F)$. Which assertions: Stacks proves 0GJA assertion by assertion from the sequence of step 4 ($H^q(C,i_*i^{-1}F)=H^q(Z,i^{-1}F)$ vanishes for $q>0$ and is the finite group $\bigoplus_{z\in Z}F_{\bar z}$ for $q=0$, unchanged by an algebraically closed extension $k'/k$; so $H^q(C,j_!j^{-1}F)\cong H^q(C,F)$ for $q\ge2$ and the five-term sequence in degrees $0,1$), so the equivalence holds for each $\mathcal C_j$ separately; for $(\mathcal C_7)$ ($C$ proper) the two five-term sequences over $k$ and $k'$ and the five lemma give $\mathcal C_7(C,F)\Leftrightarrow\mathcal C_7(C,j_!j^{-1}F)$. The node cited states the conjunction only, and this node states and uses only the conjunction; that is what its user needs (prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension proves all eight assertions together along Stacks' route and reads off $\mathcal C_7$ at the end).

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, third paragraph; Lemma 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open) and its proof

proof.text: Decomposition of $j_!j^{-1}F$ (Stacks, proof of Theorem 03SC, fourth paragraph: "$j_!\mathcal G=j_{1!}(\mathcal G|_{U_1})\oplus\dots\oplus j_{n!}(\mathcal G|_{U_n})$"). Let $\iota_a:U_a\hookrightarrow U$, so $j_a=j\circ\iota_a$. Both $j_{a,!}$ and $j_!\iota_{a,!}$ are left adjoint to $j_a^{-1}=\iota_a^{-1}j^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], so $j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})\cong j_!\iota_{a,!}\iota_a^{-1}(j^{-1}F)$; applying $j_!$ to the counit $\iota_{a,!}\iota_a^{-1}(j^{-1}F)\to j^{-1}F$ gives $\varphi_a:j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})\to j_!j^{-1}F$. Let $\varphi=\sum_a\varphi_a:\bigoplus_aj_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})\to j_!j^{-1}F$. On geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] (a stalk is a filtered colimit, so it commutes with finite direct sums), by the stalk formula of extension by zero: at $\bar x$ lying in $U_b$, the source is $(F|_{U_b})_{\bar x}=F_{\bar x}$ (the summands with $a\ne b$ vanish, as $\bar x\notin U_a$), the target is $F_{\bar x}$, and $\varphi_{\bar x}$ is the identity (the counit of $\iota_{b,!}\dashv\iota_b^{-1}$ is an isomorphism on stalks at points of $U_b$); at $\bar x$ lying in $Z$ both stalks are $0$. Hence $\varphi$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].

Finite direct sums, assertion by assertion (Stacks uses only the direction "summands $\Rightarrow$ sum", through Lemma 0A5C; the converse and the per-assertion form are written out here by the agent). Put $G_a=j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})$ and $G=\bigoplus_aG_a$. Hypotheses: all of $F$, $j_!j^{-1}F$, $G$ and the $G_a$ are sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, so each is prime to $\operatorname{char}k=p$ iff $r\ne p$ and $p$-primary iff $r=p$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]; each is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]: $G_a$ on the partition $C=U_a\sqcup(C\setminus U_a)$ (on $U_a$ it restricts to the finite locally constant $F|_{U_a}$, on the closed complement its stalks vanish by the stalk formula of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], so it restricts to $0$), and $G\cong j_!j^{-1}F$ on the partition $U_1,\dots,U_n,Z$; the hypotheses on $C$ (affine, proper) are common. So for each $j$ the hypotheses of $\mathcal C_j$ hold for $G$ iff they hold for every $G_a$. Conclusions: $H^q(C_{\Et},-)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is an additive functor, so $H^q(C,G)=\bigoplus_aH^q(C,G_a)$ via the inclusions and projections; inverse image along $\pi_{k'}:C_{k'}\to C$ and along an open immersion $b:V\hookrightarrow C$ is additive, and the pullback maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] and $b^*$ are natural in the sheaf, hence are the direct sums of those of the $G_a$. A finite direct sum of abelian groups is zero (resp. finite) iff each summand is, and a finite direct sum of homomorphisms is bijective (resp. surjective) iff each summand is. Hence $\mathcal C_j(C,G)\Leftrightarrow\mathcal C_j(C,G_a)$ for all $a$, for each $j=1,\dots,8$ [def-weil-pbc-C1], [def-weil-pbc-C2], [def-weil-pbc-C3], [def-weil-pbc-C4], [def-weil-pbc-C5], [def-weil-pbc-C6], [def-weil-pbc-C7], [def-weil-pbc-C8]; in particular for the conjunction $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] and for $\mathcal C_7$ alone.

Conclusion. Each $\mathcal C_j(C,-)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the sheaf (isomorphic sheaves have isomorphic cohomology, compatibly with the pullback maps). By step 5, $\mathcal C(C,F)\Leftrightarrow\mathcal C(C,j_!j^{-1}F)$; by step 6, $j_!j^{-1}F\cong\bigoplus_aj_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})$; by step 7, $\mathcal C(C,\bigoplus_aj_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))\Leftrightarrow\mathcal C(C,j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))$ for every $a$. This is part 3.

Replaced the one-paragraph blueprint proof by eight steps following Stacks Theorem 03SC proof (paragraphs 3-4), Lemma 0GJA and Lemma 095L: constructible bridge + generic constancy (constructible-chapter nodes, Lean closed: tools), shrinking to disjoint irreducible pieces, Z zero-dimensional, the 095L sequence (new node lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact), the 0GJA equivalence (sibling node lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-dense-open, created by the worker of prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension), the direct-sum decomposition of j_!j^{-1}F by stalks, and the per-assertion direct-sum equivalence. Repointed def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves to def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves and def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion.
